purpose: Test organ-conditioned K=5 residual experts against three study-preserving K-matched random partitions, retain the legacy row-random partition as a diagnostic, then perform a firewalled nested development-only K=1..5 specialist-count search over all organ subsets.

authorization.scope: one locked internal K5 architecture replication plus one calibration-only K search
authorization.guardrail: neither track changes or rescues any prior frozen Stage 1 or Stage 2 decision

evidence_label.reason: the study-disjoint test rows were already inspected in earlier Stage 1 analyses, and the current recovered-label snapshot contains no unused single-organ connected study groups for these five organs

data.split_integrity: connected series groups are disjoint across train, calibration, and test
data.primary_weighting: equal organ mass, then equal connected-study mass within organ

score_firewall.router_rule: replace every score-gene value with the checkpoint mask token before fitting or applying a router

partitions.legacy_random_assignment_policy: consume the already frozen row-random random_shard column exactly as a non-gating replication diagnostic

gating_random_group_k5.assignment: within each source split, assign each entire connected study to one of five shards by outcome-free deterministic bin packing that balances total and per-organ sample counts
gating_random_group_k5.gate_rule: the organ comparison must pass against every preregistered partition; do not select a favorable random partition

partitions.sealed_test_assignments: a separate hash-pinned artifact unavailable to training and K-search code

expert_training.architecture: frozen pooled trunk plus independent dimension-64 residual adapters
expert_training.checkpoint_policy: predetermined final update; no calibration checkpoint selection
expert_training.sampling: one shared deterministic natural sample schedule for both banks

router.test_router_fit: fit once on the complete calibration split, serialize and hash parameters before test inference
router.k_search_router_fit: one common five-organ router per fold; every deployed subset is a deterministic probability collapse with undeployed-organ mass mapped to other
router.k_search_nested_firewall: for each outer fold, subset selection uses four-fold inner-OOF router predictions trained only within the other four outer folds; outer-held scoring uses a router fit on those four folds

track_a_k5_internal_replication.primary_estimand: blind hard organ routing versus pooled on equal-organ/equal-study test MSE

decision.pass: internal hard-adapter K5 replication succeeds; acquire a genuinely untouched external K5 confirmation before a biological claim
decision.true_pass_blind_fail: conditional specialization exists but the observed-input router is the bottleneck
decision.random_control_fail: organ identity did not beat every study-preserving generic K5 partition; generic adapter capacity or partition variability may explain the gain
decision.pooled_fail: do not scale the organ MoE

track_b_development_k_search.definition_of_k: number of the five known organs receiving a specialist; every unselected organ uses pooled fallback
track_b_development_k_search.scope_limit: this run does not estimate the globally optimal MoE expert count, retrain K-specific banks, merge organs into K latent groups, or test K greater than five
track_b_development_k_search.subset_family: all 31 nonempty subsets of the five specialists
track_b_development_k_search.outer_selection: for each K and each of five connected-study outer folds, select the best K-organ subset using only strict inner-OOF blind MSE from the other four outer folds, then score that fixed subset with the outer-fit router on the held fold
track_b_development_k_search.final_subset_nomination: after nested performance estimation, nominate the lowest full-calibration out-of-fold-MSE subset at the selected K for a new experiment only
track_b_development_k_search.training_reuse: all K candidates reuse the same independently trained K5 organ and random expert banks; K changes deployed specialists and pooled fallback coverage, not the training partition or per-expert exposure
track_b_development_k_search.population: all five calibration organs for every K
track_b_development_k_search.fallback: pooled prediction for an unselected organ or router other class
track_b_development_k_search.matched_random_control: for each of three frozen study-preserving random K5 partitions and each outer fold, select the best of all C(5,K) random-shard subsets using only the outer-fit rows, apply pooled fallback outside that subset, and score the fixed subset on the held fold; the organ candidate must beat every partition
track_b_development_k_search.matched_random_subset_family: all C(5,K) subsets independently within each preregistered partition and outer fold
track_b_development_k_search.inference: paired connected-study sign-flip tests with clustered bootstrap effect intervals
track_b_development_k_search.multiplicity: Holm correction across five K-vs-pooled tests and separately across all fifteen K-by-study-preserving-random-partition tests
track_b_development_k_search.selection_rule: among candidates with corrected positive evidence versus pooled and random, nominate the smallest K within one standard error of the best outer-fold mean
track_b_development_k_search.interpretation: nested development nomination of deployed specialist count and subset only, not a K-specific retraining result; any nomination including K=5 requires a separately frozen retraining and untouched confirmation, and no K-search result can alter immutable Track A

requirements: at least 50 manually reviewed labels per added organ at at least 95% precision
